headline: X-Country Team Forming
transcription: A cross-country track team is now being formed. If enough people show interest dual meets with other colleges can be arranged next fall semester. Because the team is still in its planning stages, it will be considered a club and if interest remains, varsity team status is possible. This is an excellent opportunity for those who want to get into shape for the on-coming fall and spring varsity team sports. No special ability is needed, just a will to run. So if you have any interest at all please leave a note in my mailbox with your name and box number as soon as possible so a meeting can be scheduled and further details discussed. Remember this is a chance for you to: 1) Try out a new kind of experience. 2) Get into shape and stay in shape for other varsity team sports. 3) Get into competition with other colleges. Leave info in Box 329
summary: Bob Chung announces the formation of a new cross-country club at Stevens and asks interested students to contact him.
notability_note: Founding notice for what became the Stevens cross-country club.

headline: ATTENTION!
transcription: Anyone who is interested in forming a cross-country track team (especially those who were at the X-C meeting last year). There will be an organizational meeting in the 1st floor lounge of the Center on Weds. at noon. Attendance is mandatory since a recognizable number of bodies must be present so that a team can be organized and some type of competition can be scheduled for this semester. Also: Very Important! A moderator (coach, advisor, etc.) is desperately needed to keep this group together. Anyone interested or knowing someone who is interested please leave a note in Box - 329.
summary: A follow-up notice calls a mandatory organizational meeting for the cross-country club and appeals for a coach or advisor.
notability_note: Shows the club was still unformed and lacked a coach as of fall 1974.

headline: NOTICE
meet_or_event: dual meet with NCE, Oct. 9
transcription: The Stevens Cross Country running club invite everyone from the Stevens Community to its daily run (at your own comfortable pace) through a prescribed course around the campus. We meet Mon.-Fri. at 4:30 in front of the gym. P.S. this notice includes all those great athletes who want to get into shape for their prospective team sports. P.P.S. for the more serious minded runner who wants to compete; there will be a dual meet with the NCE X-C track team on Oct. 9. We'll soon have a track uniform available for those who run competitively. So come to our workouts for more info.
summary: The cross-country club invites all students to daily campus runs and announces its first dual meet, against NCE, on October 9.
notability_note: Announces the club's first-ever scheduled dual meet.

headline: Cross Country Tech Wins
meet_or_event: Dual meet vs. NCE, Branch Brook Park, Newark
transcription: In the first dual meet for the Stevens Cross Country running club, the Tech trackmen squeaked by the NCE engineers by a score of 27-32 (low score wins). The meet was held on the four-mile course at Branch Brook Park in Newark. The results of the race could not be decided until the last two runners came across the finish line. Even though the first two finishers were from NCE, a strong finish by the team proved to be the winning factor. Another element involved in our win was the fact that we had a total of eight runners, as compared to NCE's five runners. (Five is the minimum number in order to have a scoring team.) The winner of the race was NCE's Jim Johnson, who is a championship caliber runner, and proved to be too much for our first man as he finished almost three minutes ahead of our lead runner, Mike Chodnicki '78. However, a strong showing by Paul Schillinger '76 and Bob Harkins '77 gave our team the spark which ignited the victory over NCE. A point must be made in that two of our best runners did not show up, which could have provided us with a wider margin of victory than was actually recorded. A note of reminder: Everyone is welcome to run with us daily at 4:30, starting from the gym. The results for the point scorers were: Third: Mike Chodnicki '78, 25:17. Fourth: Paul Schillinger '76, 25:35. Fifth: Bob Harkins '77, 25:42. Seventh: Rich Hansen '78, 27:05. Eighth: Mike Martorano '76, 27:25.
summary: Stevens beat NCE 27-32 in its first-ever dual meet, thanks to depth (eight runners vs. NCE's five) even though NCE's Jim Johnson won individually.
notability_note: First-ever dual meet and first competitive win for the newly formed club.

headline: Spirited X-Country Team Gets 5th
meet_or_event: Cross-country relay race, Cedar Grove Park
transcription: The Stevens Tech Cross-country runners took 5th and 7th place in a cross-country relay race held in Cedar Grove Park last Sunday. Nine teams competed for the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place medals. Coach Jim Loyd entered two teams for Stevens. The members of the A team were Mike Chodnicki, Paul Schillinger, Phil Kleinlauth, and Jay Mancini. The B team runners were Steve Bies, Mike Mortarano, Rich Hansen, and Rich Kienzle. Each team member made a 2.35 mile run around the reservoir at Cedar Grove Park. Phil Kleinlauth of the A team did an exceptionally fast time of 12 min. for Stevens, averaging 5 min. 6 sec. per mile. Phil's speed and endurance brought the Stevens A team to within a couple of seconds of the 3rd place team, when the A team anchorman Jay Mancini took the baton. Jay, one of Stevens' fastest runners, was making good time for the first half of the course but unfortunately had to slacken his pace due to an injured foot, thus Stevens' A team took 5th place. Stevens' B team led by Steve Bies, captain of the cross-country runners, made a strong showing and took 7th place. Each man on both teams showed excellent school spirit and team work. Team A: Mike Chodwicki '78 12:55, Paul Schillinger '76 13:08, Phil Kleinlauth '76 12:00, Jay Mancini '76 13:20, TOTAL 51:23. Team B: Steve Bies '75 14:06, Mike Martorano '76 14:20, Rich Hansen '77 13:40, Rich Kienzle '77 14:46, TOTAL 56:52.
summary: Stevens entered two teams in a Cedar Grove Park relay of nine teams, with the A team finishing 5th and the B team 7th, led by a strong leg from Phil Kleinlauth.
confidence_notes: Runner surname appears both as 'Chodnicki' and 'Chodwicki' within the article.

headline: X Country Team Runs Marathon
meet_or_event: Fifth Philadelphia Marathon
transcription: Last Saturday, December 1, four runners from the Stevens cross-country running club represented Stevens in the Fifth Philadelphia Marathon. The weather on Sunday was cold, windy, and rainy, but still about two hundred runners showed up for the marathon of 26 miles and 385 yards. The men from Stevens were the cross country running club's coach Jim Lloyd, its captain Steve Bies '75, and members Rich Hansen '77, and Paul Schillinger '76. Due to the very bad weather conditions and other circumstances, many participants understandably did not finish the race, including two of the Stevens runners. Steve Bies had to drop from the race ¾ of the way through because of bad blisters on his feet and Rich Hansen also had to drop out ¾ of the way because of muscle cramps. Coach Lloyd and Paul Schillinger were able to finish the race with the following times: Jim Lloyd, 3 hours, 37 minutes. Paul Schillinger, 3 hours, 31 minutes. Anyone interested in running in a marathon (including women) near the end of the Christmas vacation stop by the cross country running club meeting on Wednesday, December 11 at noon in the Center, first floor lounge.
summary: Four Stevens runners competed in the Fifth Philadelphia Marathon; Bies and Hansen dropped out from injury while Lloyd and Schillinger finished.
notability_note: First marathon participation reported for the club.
confidence_notes: Slide caption dates this issue 1974-11-06, but the article text refers to events on 'December 1' and an upcoming 'December 11' meeting, which is internally inconsistent with a November 6 issue date; the deck notes this is the same article as Slide 8, whose caption date (1974-12-06) is consistent with the article text.

headline: Cross - Country Runs Asbury
meet_or_event: Asbury Park Marathon
transcription: Four Stevens Cross-country team members ran in the Asbury Park marathon on January 19. Four hundred runners started and two hundred fifty completed the 26 mile, 385 yard course, which stretched from Asbury Park to Sandy Hook and back. Of the four Stevens runners, Coach Jim Lloyd and Mike Chodwicki '78 were unable to finish because of foot and leg injuries; both ran 17 miles before they were forced to stop. Phil Kleinlauth '76, finished in 3 hours, 25 minutes and 47 seconds, and Steve Bie '75 completed the run in 3:20:04. Both runners beat the previous school record of 3:35:00 set by Paul Schillinger '75. The two Stevens men finished in 142nd and 124th place, respectively. This coming semester, the Cross-country team intends to participate in AAU sponsored track meets, as well as distance events. Anyone interested in running any distance race from 100 yards on up is welcome. An organizational meeting will be held next Wednesday, February 5, in the first floor Center lounge at 12:00 noon.
summary: Kleinlauth and Bie both broke the club's marathon record at the Asbury Park Marathon while Lloyd and Chodwicki dropped out from injury.
notability_note: Kleinlauth and Bie both beat the club's previous marathon record of 3:35:00, set by Paul Schillinger.
confidence_notes: Runner surnames appear as 'Chodwicki'/'Bie' here versus 'Chodnicki'/'Bies' elsewhere in the archive; Schillinger is credited as class of '75 here versus '76 in other slides.

headline: X-Country Runs Marathon / More Runners Welcome
meet_or_event: First Annual Newark Distance Run
transcription: Six men of the Stevens Cross-Country Running Club competed last Sunday in the First Annual Newark Distance Run which consisted of a 12-mile open race and a 4-mile run. All six men ran in the 12-mile open race which started and finished at the Newark City Hall. The course was a loop through downtown Newark and Branch Brook Park. The two races started together with about 300 runners including the Stevens runners, coach Jim Lloyd '70, club captain Steve Bies '75, Phil Kleinlauth '76, Mike Mortorano '76, Jay Mancinin '76, and Paul Schillinger '76. Surprisingly enough even the Mayor of Newark, Kenneth G. Gibson, appeared to run the 12-mile route and came in 199 out of 302 finishers. The winner of the 12-mile run was last year's Boston Marathon winner, Neil Cusack. Cusack finished the 12-mile race in 58 minutes and 38 seconds, which is very close to the world's record. The top man for Stevens was Phil Kleinlauth, '76, with the time of 1 hour, 17 minutes, and 13 seconds. Times: Phil Kleinlauth '75 1:17:13, Jay Mancinin '76 1:18:00, Steve Bies '75 1:21:34, Paul Schillinger '76 1:27:43, Jim Lloyd (coach) '70 1:28:00, Mike Martorano '76 1:31:37. Overall the 12-mile route was very good. There weren't many hills and there were plenty of officials directing the runners at the different turnoffs along the route. A special thanks goes to the police of Newark who stopped traffic whenever the runners approached intersections and kept traffic off the streets of the 12 and 4 mile loops. For those interested in running some events (including a Marathon next month) with the Stevens Cross-Country Club, there are meetings held each Wednesday at 12 noon in the 1st floor lounge in the Center (women are also invited).
summary: Six Stevens runners ran the 12-mile First Annual Newark Distance Run, whose field included Newark's mayor and Boston Marathon winner Neil Cusack; Kleinlauth was Stevens' top finisher.
notability_note: Race field included reigning Boston Marathon champion Neil Cusack and Newark mayor Kenneth Gibson.
confidence_notes: The article text lists Phil Kleinlauth as class of '76 in the prose but '75 in the results table; both readings are preserved as printed.

headline: Cross-Country Loses Despite Excellent Efforts
meet_or_event: Dual meets vs. Montclair State, Ramapo, West Point Prep, Bergen Community College
transcription: Trying to build on the foundation started last year, the Stevens Tech Cross Country team opened up its season with intercollegiate competition with Montclair State, Ramapo, West Point Prep and Bergen Community College. The first meet was held October 1 with Ramapo and Montclair, over the rocky and hilly 4.6 mile Ramapo College course. Despite a game try, Stevens was soundly beaten by Montclair 15 to 48 (low score wins) and edged by Ramapo (22 to 37). Still, a promising performance was turned in by Phil Kleinlauth '76, whose time of 25:53 beat all of the Ramapo runners and was just 45 seconds behind the first place Montclair State runner. On October 18, the Stevens harriers ran against West Point Prep and Bergen Community. The 5 mile course at Bergen, which was run in the pouring rain, became a quagmire with a lot of it run through ankle deep ponds. Stevens again suffered losses to West Point Prep 18 to 45 and Bergen 20 to 41. Phil finished third in the race, beating everyone from Bergen Community with time of 29:28. Good races were also turned in by Mike Chodnicki '78, Steven Zell '78, Mike Martorano '76, and Jim McCann '78. Coach Jim Lloyd looks optimistically to Stevens next meet with N.J.I.T. at Branch Brook Park. Anyone interested in joining the team should contact Phil Kleinlauth Box 625 or Jim Lloyd, Metallurgy Department.
summary: Stevens opened its 1975 intercollegiate cross-country schedule with losses to Montclair State, Ramapo, West Point Prep, and Bergen Community, though Kleinlauth ran strong individual times.

transcription: It is nice to see that the school is finally realizing the problem in the Gym facilities here at Stevens. They will be making many needed improvements, and the only other improvement we can see that should be made is to resurface the track. The track is very hard and slippery, and could possibly be resurfaced with a rubber type compound.
summary: An editorial fragment welcomes planned gym improvements and calls for the track surface to be resurfaced.
confidence_notes: Only a fragment of this article/editorial is visible in the crop.

headline: Track Club
meet_or_event: Second Annual Newark Distance Run
transcription: This past Sunday, the Stevens Track Club competed in the second annual Newark Distance Run. Two separate races were held at the same time, one being 4.3 miles long and the other 12 miles long. The courses start at the YMCA on Broad Street and Central Avenue. They continue along Broad Street, with the 4 miles course looping back, and the 12 mile race continuing through Branch Brook Park before heading back to the “Y.” This year's races had its largest competitor's field ever of 700 runners. The field was of outstanding quality due to the fact that this is an Olympic year and many good long distance runners are looking to qualify for the Olympic Trials this summer in either the 10,000 meters or marathon. A total of 350 runners finished the 4 mile course and 308 finished the 12 mile course. Mike Chodnicki, class of '78, ran an excellent time of 26:40, finishing 70th in the 4 mile race. Mike Maratano, class of '76 followed him with a time of 29:17, placing 131st. Steven Zell, class of '78 ran the 12 mile course in 1:21:10, finishing 165th, not bad for the first time ever running this distance. Captain Phil Kleinlauth, class of '76 had a time of 1:14:46 finishing 108th. Special thanks must be given to Mrs. Stanley Chadnicki, who has become a fixture at the Stevens Track Club's events. Her cheers of encouragement during a race and words of congratulations or consolation after a race are deeply appreciated. Anyone interested in joining the Track Club either on a competitive level or just to jog to get into shape should contact Phil Kleinlauth, box 625. Meetings are held every Wednesday at 12:00 in the Center Lounge.
summary: Four Stevens Track Club members ran the second annual Newark Distance Run in a record 700-runner field, an Olympic-year event.

headline: Runners Take Second Place Honors
meet_or_event: U.S. Track and Field Federation 15km relay, Cedar Grove, N.J.
transcription: The Stevens Track Club ran second, winning silver medals in the U.S. Track and Field Federation's 15 kilometer relay at Cedar Grove, N.J. this past Sunday. The race was run around the Cedar Grove reservoir with each member running 2.35 miles. The team's time of 52.09 placed them behind the North Jersey Student Track Club who were a distant third. The race was exciting right down to the closing miles. Phil Kleinlauth '76 led the team to a 59 second lead over their nearest competitor with a 12.13 opening leg. Steven Zell, '78, running in his first competitive race for Stevens, ran a game third leg of 13:45, but was not strong enough to hold off the closing kick of the Striders' club runner. Mike Chodnicki, '78 anchoring the relay, tried desperately to regain the lead, but could not. His time was an excellent 13:09. Other members running well for Stevens were Hampton Sailer, '77, Mike Martorano '76 and Paul Schillinger '76.
summary: The Stevens Track Club took silver medals in the USTFF 15km relay at Cedar Grove after leading for much of the race before being overtaken late.
notability_note: Team won silver medals at the U.S. Track and Field Federation 15km relay championship.
confidence_notes: The same clipping/photo also shows an unrelated notice ('To All Varsity and JV players') about a Stevens Athletic Association awards assembly; that content is off-topic (not XC/track-specific) and was not transcribed.

headline: Track Team Seeks Runners
transcription: The Stevens Track Team is starting its third season and is looking for new members. We have run marathons in Philadelphia and New Jersey along with the annual twelve mile Greater Newark Race and other numerous road races. Last year we competed in intercollegiate cross-country against Bergen Community, Ramapo, Montclair State, West Point Prep and N.J. Institute of Technology. We are interested in all people: the person wanting to get into shape for other sports, the casual jogger interested in physical fitness and losing weight or the serious competitor interested in running road races as well as competing in intercollegiate cross-country. Our practices are held on campus as well as in the scenic streets of Hoboken and Jersey City. The club is open to male and female undergraduate and graduate students. The last meeting was held Wednesday, September 22 in the first floor Center lounge at 12:00 noon. Anyone interested in running should contact Phil Kleinlauth Box #1170 or Jim Lloyd c/o Metallurgy Dept.
summary: A recruiting notice for the club's third season recaps its marathon and cross-country history and invites all students, including women, to join.
notability_note: Confirms the club, now called the Track Team, was in its third season and open to men and women.

headline: Newark Parks Test Runners
meet_or_event: Dual meet vs. N.J.I.T., Branch Brook Park, Newark
transcription: The Stevens cross-country team opened its season last Wednesday with a 20-35 loss to NJIT (low score wins). The meet was held at Branch Brook Park in Newark over a 4.3 mile course. Phil Kleinlauth was the first Stevens runner across the finish line, finishing third overall with a time of 23:20. Steven Zell '78 ran an excellent race finishing fifth with a time of 24:27. The other scorers for Stevens were Mike Chadnicki '78, Tom Gardener '78, Joe Tomezyh '80, John Sharkey '78, and Mary Doddy '80. Mary is the first woman in Stevens intercollegiate history to compete against male competition. The squad hopes to even its record to 1-1 when it races against Jersey City State at Bayonne Park next week.
summary: Stevens opened its 1976 cross-country season with a 20-35 loss to NJIT; the roster included Mary Doddy, the first woman to compete in Stevens intercollegiate athletics against men.
notability_note: Mary Doddy is reported as the first woman in Stevens intercollegiate history to compete against male competition.

headline: Cross Country Off To Slow Start
meet_or_event: Dual meet vs. Jersey City State; I.A.C. Championship vs. Drew and N.J.I.T.
transcription: The Stevens Cross Country Club lived up to its nickname of the Ducks on October 20 when it took on Jersey City State in the pouring rain at Bayonne Park. The rain coupled with the muddy terrain and lack of familiarity with the course led to the Ducks downfall of 18-37. Phill Kleinlauth went out with the early leaders, but faded to third near the closing stages of the 4.75 mile race, making the best showing for Stevens with a time of 24:43. Strong races turned in by Steven Zell '78, and Ian Howe '80, with times of 26:22 and 26:49 respectively, were bright spots in an otherwise dismal day. Other runners for Stevens included Mike Chadnicki '78, Tom Gardener '78, John Sharkey '78 and Mary Doddy '80. On October 23, the club participated in the I.A.C. championship with Drew and N.J.I.T. over the 4.3 mile course at Branch Brook Park, Newark. Again Stevens wound up on the short end of the score losing to Drew 18-37 and to N.J.I.T., 16-49. However, marked improvements were turned in by the whole team. Steven Zell '78, was the first finisher for Stevens finishing 5th in the field of 18 with a time of 24:20. The team will be looking for its first win, Wednesday, November 3, when it takes on Bergen Community College.
summary: Stevens, nicknamed the Ducks, lost to Jersey City State and then to both Drew and NJIT at the I.A.C. championship, though the team showed improvement.

headline: Runners End Fall Season
meet_or_event: Dual meets vs. Bergen Community College and Ramapo College
transcription: The Stevens Cross Country Club ran November 3rd against Bergen Community College, at Paramus, N.J. Stevens wound up on the short end of the score losing 23-32. The race was held over Bergen's 5.2 mile course which consisted of many rolling hills and winding paths. Phil Kleinlauth placed second in the race for Stevens with a time of 29:53. Steven Zell, '78, placed fifth overall with a time of 31:55. Ian Howe, '80, and Tom Gardener, '78, placed seventh and eight respectively. John Sharkey, '78, was running well for Stevens, but fell going down a steep hill and failed to finish. The Cross Country Club ended their season on a losing note to Ramapo College, 23-32, at Ramapo on November 13. The course was a rugged 4.6 miles over harsh terrain with frequent hills, rocks, and trees hindering the runner's path. The last part of the race was a long winding downhill section with numerous loose rocks, making footing very treacherous. Stevens hopes for victory were dashed when Ian Howe, '80, and David Zitz, '80, fell while hurdling a huge boulder in their path. On the bright side, Phil Kleinlauth won the race with a time of 25:47. Steve Zell, '78, grabbed fourth with Tom Gardener and John Sharkey eighth and ninth respectively. Although the club's record for the year was 0-6, this does not reflect the effort put forth by the team. They are just a club in it's embryonic stages and found themselves up against varsity teams with fulltime paid coaches. These schools also had their own home racing courses and practice tracks. Stevens, on the other hand, uses the paved streets of Hoboken to practice. The team would like to run a track and field schedule intercollegiately, but needs more members for the winter months. Anyone interested please contact Phil Kleinlauth, Box 1170.
summary: Stevens closed its 0-6 fall 1976 season with losses to Bergen Community and Ramapo, though Kleinlauth won the individual race at Ramapo.

headline: Track Club Wants You!
transcription: The Stevens Track Club is looking for more new members. This fall they completed their cross country program. Although it was not successful looking at the win-loss column, it was successful in that Stevens succeeded in being competitive with other colleges having larger teams and better facilities. We hope to build on this foundation and possibly compete in track and field. We are looking for sprinters, distancemen, weight-throwers, or anyone else who has a passing fancy to keep in shape. The team needs undergraduates and graduate students, both men and women. Anyone interested should contact Phil Kleinlauth, Box #1170 or attend the next Track Club meeting on Wednesday, February 9th at 12 noon in the Center Lounge.
summary: A recruiting notice looks back on the completed cross-country season and calls for new members, including sprinters and throwers, to build a track and field program.
notability_note: Signals the club's intent to expand from cross country into track and field events.

headline: Trackmen Open with good showing
meet_or_event: N.J.T.F.F. Track and Field Indoor Championship, East Stroudsburg State College
transcription: The Stevens Track Club traveled to East Stroudsburg State College in Pennsylvania this past Sunday to run in the N.J.T.F.F. Track and Field Indoor Championship. Although the club did not win any medals, it still came up with some fine performances. John Sharkey tripled in the meet, running a 7.1 second 60 yd. dash, 1:30.5 in the 600 yard run, and 26.8 seconds in the 220. Ian Howe just missed out on a 4th place medal with a lunging dive at the tape in the 440. He finished with a time of 2:34 followed by Jim Maroney's 2:47. Mike Chodnicki and Steve Zell ran the mile in times of 4:53 and 5:00 respectively. Phil Kleinlauth ran the 3 mile in a time of 16:50. Anyone interested in running should drop a note in box 1170 or come to the Wednesday meetings at 12 noon in the Center Lounge.
summary: The Stevens Track Club competed in its first indoor track and field championship at East Stroudsburg, coming away without medals but with solid individual times.
confidence_notes: Ian Howe's reported 440 time of 2:34 appears inconsistent with a typical 440-yard time (closer to a half-mile/880 time); preserved as printed since exact event/time pairing could not be confirmed.

headline: Tech Track News
meet_or_event: New Jersey Federation Track Meet and Championship Meet, Cedar Grove
transcription: On Sunday, October 2 Steven's Track Club ran in the New Jersey Federation Track Meet and Championship Meet at Cedar Grove. In the 4.7 mile race Ian Howe '80 ran a strong race, saving a little bit too much for the end, causing him to lose a third place medal. He took fourth with a time of 28:07:28 minutes. John Sharkey (senior) runs a strong race each time he races. He took sixth with the time of 28:32:41 minutes. Jim Maroney (sophomore) running with the team for the first time gave an excellent performance, taking tenth in a time of 30:33 minutes. Mike Chodnicki (senior) was off this day but still beat half of the field running 30:45:7 minutes. You can't really blame him too much because it was pouring rain all morning making conditions hazardous for running. The highlight of the meet was the championship race in which Stevens entered Phil Kleinlauth. Phil has been Tech's best runner for the past three years, and he proved his abilities once again in this 5000 meter race. The race was started with strong competition, but Phil went out with the leaders and brought home the third place bronze in a time of 16:31:82 minutes. The overall outcome of this meet was very good. In upcoming meets Tech Track plans to run more and more races this well and better. If you are interested in joining the team contact Mike Chodnicki, Box 197 or just come to the Center first floor lounge any Wednesday at 12:00 noon.
summary: At the New Jersey Federation meet, Howe, Sharkey, Maroney, and Chodnicki placed well in the 4.7 mile race while Phil Kleinlauth won bronze in the 5000 meter championship race.
notability_note: Phil Kleinlauth won an individual bronze medal in the 5000 meter championship race.
confidence_notes: A separate, partially cropped item ('IDC Sports', about the start of IDC fall sports) appears on the same slide; it is unrelated to XC/track and was not transcribed beyond noting it here. Several times are printed in an unusual minutes:seconds:hundredths-like format (e.g. 28:07:28); reproduced as printed.

headline: Runners Lose Quad Meet, Beat N.J.I.T. at Newark
meet_or_event: Dual meet vs. N.J.I.T., Branch Brook Park; 5-mile I.A.C. Championship, Drew University
transcription: The Stevens Cross Country Team started their busy racing week last Wednesday with their first ever victory over N.J.I.T. 20-35 (low score wins) at Branch Brook Park, Newark. The course was 4.3 miles and the race was held in the pouring rain. Jim Noctor of N.J.I.T. was first in a time of 23:13. Newcomer, Gary Melone '79, ran an outstanding race finishing second in a time of 23:32 for Stevens. He was followed by Phil Kleinlauth in 23:40, John Sharkey '79 in 25:59, Jim Maroney '80 in 26:16 and Jim Weixel '80 in 26:32. This past Saturday, Stevens traveled to Madison, N.J. to the campus of Drew University to run in the 5 mile I.A.C. Championship. The race was held over a rocky and challenging course which was very treacherous due to heavy rains the night before. Two Stevens runners, Mike Chodnicki '78 and Jim Weixel, were forced to quit during the race due to turned ankles. John Sharkey ran an excellent race placing 9th for Stevens, while Jim Maroney ran 13th. Unfortunately this was not enough as Stevens wound up on the short end of the score against Drew, N.J.I.T. and Brooklyn Poly.
summary: Stevens beat N.J.I.T. for the first time ever in a rainy dual meet, then lost the I.A.C. Championship at Drew, where two runners dropped out with turned ankles.
notability_note: First-ever cross-country dual meet victory over N.J.I.T.

headline: Track Club
meet_or_event: New Jersey Track Federation Championships, East Stroudsburg State College
transcription: On Sunday, March 12, the Stevens Track Club ventured to East Stroudsburg State College in East Stroudsburg, Pennsylvania, for the New Jersey Track Federation Championships. Entered in the 2 mile run were Phil Kleinlauth (grad student) and Abdallah Sadadui 81. This was Abdul's first race ever and the novice in him hampered his position, but his spirit caused him to run a fine time of 11:43. Phil was a little off form but his being a veteran of track easily gave him a good time of 11:08. In the 1000 yard run, Ian Howe 80 was entered. He went out with the leaders and ran a strong race bettering his time of last year 2:38 to 2:33.1. He took fourth in his race.
summary: At the NJ Track Federation Championships, Kleinlauth and first-time racer Sadadui ran the 2-mile, and Ian Howe improved his 1000-yard time to take fourth.

headline: RUNNERS COLUMN
meet_or_event: Jersey Journal Cross Country Race, Lincoln Park
transcription: Freshman Al Alonso and Senior Ian Howe represented Stevens Cross Country Club in the Jersey Journal Cross Country Race, Sunday, September 30. Alonso finished the 2½ mile course third in 13:51, and Howe finished fourth in 14:16.5 on the Lincoln Park Course. If anyone is interested in running, please contact Al Alonso (Box 42) for any distance. The club is approximately 20 strong including its first manager, Nancy Pizzino. Training will begin soon for the indoor season.
summary: Alonso and Howe placed third and fourth at the Jersey Journal Cross Country Race, and the roughly 20-member club named its first manager, Nancy Pizzino.

headline: Runners column
meet_or_event: Dual meet vs. N.J.I.T., Branch Brook Park; Jersey Journal Mini Marathon
transcription: The Stevens Cross Country Club took to hill and dale this past weekend in their efforts to overcome back to back races in 40 degree weather. Saturday Stevens and N.J.I.T. battled out a dual meet which ended in a win/lost margin of only 5 points. Stevens finished up on the short end placing 2,4,6,8,10, and 11 with N.J.I.T. finishing 1,3,5,7,9--very close. Our first three finishers clocked very good times of 23:39 (Al Alonso '83), 24:16 (Ian Howe, '80), and 24:36 (Dave Arbeitel, '83); averaging 5:01, 5:09, 5:14 (per mile) respectfully. The race was 4.7 miles at Branch Brooke Park. Tight and sore from the day before, on Sunday Alonso and Howe braved the weather once more. At the race's end, they completed the 7.5 mile Jersey Journal Mini Marathon along with some 400 other runners. Alonso finished 15 in 44:07 and Howe 17 in 44:55. The club will represent Stevens in the Independent Athletic Conference championship cross country race at Garrett Mountain this Saturday (Oct. 20). If anyone is interested in running for the club in future meets contact Al Alonso, Box 42.
summary: Stevens narrowly lost a dual meet to N.J.I.T. by 5 points, then Alonso and Howe backed it up the next day by finishing the 7.5-mile Jersey Journal Mini Marathon.

headline: Runners column
meet_or_event: I.A.C. Cross Country Championship, Garrett Mountain; dual meet at Ramapo College
transcription: In their bid to capture the I.A.C. Cross Country Championship, Saturday, October 20, at Garrett Mountain. Stevens Cross Country Club met us with an unfortunate accident and sickness. Star freshman Dave Arbeitel fell ill to food poisoning, yet he and Keith Moore were still there to urge on the rest of the team. The race started out fast and tightly packed. This resulted in an N.J.I.T. runner loosing his footing on loose, rocky ground; at that point, senior member Ian Howe twisted an old hamstring pull in an attempt to avoid a [text missing between the source crops] continued the race anyway and completed it. The rest of the clubs' runners ran extremely well as a result. The final standing went as follows: 1),5),8),11),14),16), -- Drew, first ---2),6),9),10),17), --N.J.I.T., second ---3 Fernando, 4) Alonso, 7)Howe, 13)Haas, 20)Maatsch, --Stevens, third---12),15),18),19),21)---N.Y. Polytechnic, fourth---Yeshiva, forfeited last. A hypothetical finish, according to past times and under better conditions, the final would very realistically have read: Drew-43, NJIT-46; Stevens-36; N.Y. Poly.-90. The actual finish read as follows: Drew-39; NJIT-44; Stevens-47; N.Y. Poly.-85; Yeshiva-forfeit last. Drew vs NJIT-26-30; Drew vs Stevens-27-28; Drew vs N.Y. Poy-16-39; Stevens vs NJIT-28-27; Stevens vs N.Y. Poly.-20-35; Personal times for Saturday: Fernando (27:02), Alonso (27:49) Howe (28:49), Haas (33:08), Maatsch (38:24) for 5 miles distance. This was Fernando's first outing for the team; a well trained runner out of Union Hill, along with Alonso, hopefully will be a permanent addition to what is turning into a very tough squad. There was only 1 point difference between Drew and Stevens and NJIT and Stevens. The scores speak for themselves under healthier and safer conditions Stevens could have won hands down running just average. Wednesday, October 24, the club took to the hills of Ramapo College, one of the most dangerous around. Short their #1 and #4 runners due to injury and illness, they took up the challenge anyway. Al Alonso won in 36:54. Howe placed third on the 10,000 meter (6.2 miles) course in 38:17). The rest of the club placed six, ninth and tenth. Ramapo won 26 to 29; once again due to misfortune's of Saturday.
summary: At the I.A.C. championship at Garrett Mountain, Stevens finished third despite illness, injury (including Ian Howe re-injuring a hamstring), and only narrowly lost to Drew and NJIT; days later a short-handed squad lost narrowly to Ramapo.
notability_note: Team finished within one point of both Drew and NJIT at the I.A.C. championship despite illness and injury to key runners.

headline: Runners Column
meet_or_event: Y.M.C.A. Fitness Run, Hoboken
transcription: Saturday October 27, the Cross Country Club took part in what turned out to be a Stevens ‘family affair’. Outside of the club, other participants were Dr. Don Sebastion, Heidi Meyer ('81), a teacher assistant, and the graduate assistant to the basketball team. The Y.M.C.A. Fitness Run covered the outskirts of Hoboken totaling 5 miles. Al Alonso ('83) finished 6th in a time of 26:27, Ian Howe ('80) finished 8th in a time of 27:21, the rest of the club finished in the top quarter of the race; which totaled 194 persons. Alonso took the gold in the 13-18 year old category; Heidi took the bronze medal in the women 19-29 year old category.
summary: Stevens runners and staff took part in the Hoboken Y.M.C.A. Fitness Run as a group, with Alonso and Meyer both winning age-group medals.
notability_note: Al Alonso and Heidi Meyer won age-group medals (gold and bronze respectively) at the Fitness Run.

headline: Runners column
meet_or_event: Weehawken Mini-marathon
transcription: Sunday, November 4th, members of the Stevens Cross Country Club and Stevens community took part in Weehawkin's Mini-marathon race. The first finisher was senior member Ian Howe who finished fourth overall and first in his age group (21 and up). His time of 26:10 earned him a first place trophy. Al Alonso ('81) was the second Stevens cross country club finisher, and Bill Maatsch ('80) was the third. Graduate student Steve Teslik, who this year completed the New York Marathon, ran very well along with Prof. Don Sebastian.
summary: Ian Howe finished fourth overall and won his age group and a trophy at the Weehawken Mini-marathon, leading a group of Stevens runners and community members.
notability_note: Ian Howe won his age group and a first-place trophy.
